package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of a legitimate library and, upon execution, downloads and runs a remote executable (DiscordRAT 2.0), which enables remote access, data exfiltration, and further malware deployment (r77 rootkit and Blank-Grabber infostealer). The package is designed to mimic a legitimate package to trick users into installing malware, resulting in full system compromise, persistence, and theft of sensitive information.

execution_context.file_location: main entry point (e.g., index.js or main.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates an HTTP request to download a remote executable (DiscordRAT 2.0), writes the binary to disk, and executes it as a new process, resulting in the installation of a remote access trojan on the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a remote binary without user consent, a hallmark of malware delivery. This behavior is not expected in any legitimate npm package and directly exposes the system to remote compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not fetch and execute remote binaries as part of their normal operation, especially without explicit user notification and consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters or installers may download and run binaries, but this is always disclosed, typically signed, and never occurs silently in a package's main entry point.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after DiscordRAT execution, via command from C2)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DiscordRAT receives command to download and execute r77 rootkit; modifies registry keys to hide process.
malicious_snippets.code_language: windows binary (C# or C++), registry manipulation
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after receiving a command from the attacker's C2, the DiscordRAT payload downloads the r77 rootkit, executes it, and modifies specific Windows registry keys to hide its process and executable path, achieving stealth and persistence on the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Deploying a rootkit to hide malware presence is a hallmark of advanced persistent threats and is never legitimate in userland packages. Registry manipulation for process hiding is a clear indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not install rootkits or manipulate registry keys to hide processes or executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate use cases for rootkit deployment or registry-based process hiding in npm packages.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after DiscordRAT execution, via command from C2)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DiscordRAT receives commands to exfiltrate data, disable security software, kill processes, block input devices, or shut down the system.
malicious_snippets.code_language: windows binary (C# or C++), system API calls
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, under remote operator control, the RAT executes commands to collect and exfiltrate system information, disable or tamper with security software, terminate running processes, block mouse and keyboard input, or forcibly shut down the system, resulting in full system compromise and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: These are classic remote access trojan (RAT) capabilities, enabling attackers to fully control the victim system, steal data, and disrupt normal operation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should provide remote operators with the ability to exfiltrate data, disable security, or control system input/output.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools in enterprise environments may have similar capabilities, but are never distributed as public npm packages and always require explicit user consent and configuration.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (in most recent two versions, after DiscordRAT execution)
execution_context.file_location: main entry point (e.g., index.js or main.js)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, in the latest two versions, the code downloads a PyInstaller-compiled Blank-Grabber infostealer from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it as a new process, resulting in the collection and exfiltration of sensitive user data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing an infostealer directly threatens user privacy and security, as it is designed to harvest and exfiltrate sensitive information without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should ever download and execute an infostealer or any binary that collects and exfiltrates user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate use cases for infostealer deployment in npm packages.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package, which mimics a legitimate one.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code execution upon import or use.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package downloads and executes DiscordRAT 2.0 from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is infected with a remote access trojan.

attack_chain.action: DiscordRAT establishes a channel with the attacker's Discord server and awaits commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can remotely control the infected system.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands to exfiltrate data, disable security, kill processes, block input, or shut down the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise, data theft, and potential denial of service.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues command to deploy r77 rootkit, which hides the malware's presence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence and stealth on the victim system.

attack_chain.action: In the latest versions, the package also downloads and executes Blank-Grabber infostealer.

behavioral_signatures: NPM package downloads and executes remote binaries at runtime without user consent
Establishes outbound connections to Discord servers for command and control (C2)
Deploys rootkit by modifying specific Windows registry keys for process hiding
Executes infostealer payloads (Blank-Grabber) after initial infection
Creates new processes from downloaded executables
file_indicators: Presence of discordrat.exe or similarly named binaries in temporary or user directories
Registry subkeys and values associated with r77 rootkit (e.g., HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options)
blank-grabber.exe or other unexpected executables dropped by npm packages
Unusual executable files created in %TEMP% or user profile directories after package installation
network_indicators: Outbound connections to Discord API/domains (e.g., discord.com, discordapp.com)
HTTP(S) requests to remote file hosting domains used for malware payloads (e.g., remote-server.com)
Connections to known C2 infrastructure associated with DiscordRAT or Blank-Grabber
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for unexpected network activity, especially HTTP(S) requests to download executables. Flag packages that fetch and execute remote binaries at runtime. Detect creation or modification of suspicious registry keys linked to rootkit persistence (e.g., r77). Watch for outbound connections to Discord or other C2 channels from developer environments. Alert on the presence of known malware binaries (DiscordRAT, r77, Blank-Grabber) in user or temp directories, and registry modifications typical of rootkits. Correlate process creation events with npm package execution to identify suspicious child processes.
